subjects.authored_statement: The installable Python distribution, import package, executable command, generated report brand, supported environment variables, documentation, tests, fixtures that describe current interfaces, and GitHub workflows use RepoDelta consistently.
A fresh installation exposes repodelta and does not require or advertise a prismcode executable or import package.
Supported LLM and workflow configuration uses the REPODELTA_ namespace.
Generated HTML and newly generated artifacts identify RepoDelta without changing deterministic review semantics.
Current documentation distinguishes the temporary GitHub installation path from the future PyPI repodelta release.
Repository checks fail if a stale supported PrismCode product identity or live import/command path is reintroduced.
Preserve historical PR, Issue, commit, and recorded campaign evidence rather than rewriting their original source text or old repository paths.
Do not change review, assessment, graph, LLM-shadow, or security semantics as part of the rename.
Do not rename the GitHub repository before the rename tree is merged; existing links must remain usable during the transition.
Do not claim that the PyPI package, GitHub organization, or domain has been reserved until registration actually succeeds.

Rewriting historical GitHub records and recorded evidence, purchasing a domain, publishing to PyPI, renaming or transferring the GitHub repository, and changing product behavior beyond identity migration.

The distribution, Python package, CLI, environment variables, generated HTML, workflows, documentation, and README assets still exposed the crowded PrismCode name. A mechanical global rewrite would also falsify frozen evaluation packets, source provenance, and historical PR/Issue references.
publishes the distribution and Python package as repodelta version 0.1.0;
exposes only the repodelta CLI and REPODELTA_LLM_ configuration surface;
migrates imports, runtime identifiers, temporary workspace/ref namespaces, workflows, tests, generated HTML branding, docs, license text, links, and README assets;
updates onboarding to the future repodelta/repodelta repository identity and a one-time isolated pipx installation;
regenerates the README overview from a real report produced by the renamed package;
adds a repository identity gate that rejects stale supported identity while explicitly allowing provenance and frozen evaluation artifacts;
preserves historical repository names, paths, PR/Issue URLs, and labeling/observation packets where changing them would alter evidence identity.
This is an intentional clean pre-launch break. There is no legacy executable, import package, or environment-variable alias.
